evidence.quote: “Hush! Wait.” She crept to the top of the ladder and listened.
“Leave it to me.” To his amazement, Tommy saw that she was fastening

adjudications.reason: In the draft, Annette's 'Quick--up here!' and 'Hush! Wait.' sit in consecutive paragraphs. Her peep-hole line is then followed by a new paragraph, 'Leave it to me.', so the speaker changes are unclear. The string-pull also follows Conrad's question directly, so the decoy logic is never stated: the men must believe he went up because he did not pass them. The plan flags these attic mechanics as a risk. The fix is to restore Tommy's two prompts and the German's exchange from the source.

evidence.quote: She raised a hand and turned out the light.
her action with the light, he came to the conclusion that the room was overlooked

adjudications.reason: Every essential beat survives: she turns out the light, delivers the mockery (V6) and passes the knife. Tommy's later inference from 'her action with the light' still has its basis in the draft. Losing the verbal cover is a legitimate tradeoff, and restoring it would cost about 30 words against a reduction target.

evidence.quote: Tommy had run back to the stairs. Then his heart sank.
He would not go without her.

adjudications.reason: Partly confirmed. In the draft, 'Tommy had run back to the stairs' has no stated motive, because the line saying he would not leave without her was cut. Restoring that one source sentence is cheap. Tommy's defence of Annette to Carter is not essential: the plan only requires Carter's view that she belongs to the gang. The cry itself stays intact and unexplained.

evidence.quote: But they must have found out about me suddenly in some way.
The curious thing is that they certainly did not know anything about you when they first held you prisoner.

adjudications.reason: The puzzle survives without this passage. The draft keeps Tommy's wrong police guess, Carter's denial, the 'twigged' line, the Ritz possibility and 'they must have found out about me suddenly'. Revised 020 also keeps Sir James's 'did not know anything about you'. The self-check passage strengthens the puzzle but is not needed for it.

evidence.quote: “You have _not_ used Pear’s soap, I see.”
“Nothing,” said Tommy, “could be plainer than your words--unless it was your face.”

adjudications.reason: The plan says one Conrad exchange is enough, and the Pear's soap jab plus 'It's little enough time' supply it. Tommy's banter also survives in 'plainer than your words--unless it was your face' and 'wherefore the bonds and fetters'. Restoring more would work against the required reduction, so this is a legitimate tradeoff.

remaining_concerns: Estimated net change is about -40 to -42 words; code should verify. If the result runs a few words over, ', which was one satisfaction' style trims are unavailable, so the next optional cut would be '--very little time indeed'.
